issues.description: Fields 'lectureName' and 'numberOfInscribedStudents' in class Lecture have different access modifiers across artifacts. In the template (src/de/tum/cit/ase/Lecture.java lines 4-5) these two fields are declared public: 'public String lectureName;' and 'public int numberOfInscribedStudents;'. In the problem statement UML (problem_statement.md lines 64-68) the attributes are shown as private (leading '-' in the UML) and the solution implementation (solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Lecture.java lines 6-10) declares all lecture attributes (lectureName, numberOfInscribedStudents, numberOfGuestStudents, numberOfLecturers, numberOfTutors) as private. This mismatch can confuse students about the intended encapsulation and whether they should implement getters/setters (public fields remove the need for accessors and contradict the UML/solution expectation).
issues.suggestedFix: Make the visibility of the fields in the template match the UML and solution: change the existing declarations in src/de/tum/cit/ase/Lecture.java to private (e.g. 'private String lectureName;' and 'private int numberOfInscribedStudents;'). If you want the template to still require students to add the remaining attributes, keep the TODO markers for adding those fields but ensure any provided example fields use private visibility so students implement getters/setters as intended. This preserves the pedagogical goal (students implement accessors) while removing the confusing public-field exposure.
